title: JSON

exercises.title: Serialize a struct
exercises.description: Build a JSON object for `Name=Alice`, `Age=30` and Console.WriteLine it with stable key order (`Name` then `Age`).
hints: Insert keys in emission order (`Name` before `Age`) into `Dictionary<string, object>` on modern runtime.
`JsonSerializer.Serialize` handles primitive boxing cleanly.
Import `System.Text.Json` namespaces explicitly.

exercises.title: Deserialize JSON
exercises.description: Parse `{"Name":"Bob","Age":25}` and Console.WriteLine `Bob 25` on one line.
hints: `JsonDocument.Parse` + `RootElement.GetProperty("Name")` is lightweight structured access.
Dispose `JsonDocument` with `using` for deterministic cleanup.

exercises.title: Property names
hints: Dictionary keys dictate JSON naming—use literals like `first_name` verbatim.
No renaming policy necessary when dictionaries drive serialization.

exercises.title: Omit nulls
exercises.description: Serialize only `Server` with value `api.example.com` (capital `S`), omitting unset fields.
hints: `JsonSerializerOptions.DefaultIgnoreCondition = JsonIgnoreCondition.WhenWritingNull` drops empty fields.
Populate only non-null dictionary entries contributing to payload.

exercises.title: Round trip
exercises.description: Serialize a product `{id:1,name:Laptop,price:999.99}` camelCase, deserialize, and Console.WriteLine two lines with the C#-style brace formatting.
hints: Toggle `PropertyNamingPolicy = JsonNamingPolicy.CamelCase` for CLR→JSON bridging.
Round-trip through `Deserialize<Dictionary<string, JsonElement>>` when dynamic shapes persist.
Invariant culture keeps prices aligned when stringifying decimals/doubles manually.

exercises.title: Nested structs
exercises.description: Serialize nested `User` with PascalCase keys matching the checker output.
hints: Nest dictionaries to express structured JSON subtrees.
Serialize outer container once inner maps are hydrated.

exercises.title: Encode a slice
exercises.description: Serialize a JSON array with two people objects.
hints: `List<Dictionary<string, object>>` becomes a JSON array of objects sequentially.
Keep person property ordering consistent inside each dictionary.

exercises.title: Deferred nested JSON
exercises.description: Parse nested JSON, Console.WriteLine `level`, then Console.WriteLine the nested `data` object using `GetRawText()` to preserve key order.
hints: Use `.GetRawText()` on nested `JsonElement`s to preserve key ordering verbatim.
Print scalar properties before dumping nested fragments if instructions demand layering.

exercises.title: Decode an array
exercises.description: Parse a JSON array of people and Console.WriteLine `Name Age` per line.
hints: Enumerate `.RootElement.EnumerateArray()` for loosely typed parses.
Read UTF-16 property names (`Name`, `Age`) via `GetProperty(...).GetString()` / `.GetInt32()`.
